comments.body:
Implemented the force-bypass unification. Pushed as Gerrit change 1878 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1878), commit fe4281e07c, trailer rebar-ticket:73b2-6194-c430-45ab.

Scope landed:
- _lib_writes.transition -> force: str|None; _normalize_transition_force folds retired force_close=<r> and force=True to warn+map deprecation aliases (registered in _deprecations.py). claim threads force as the unified reason.
- transition_compute: three-way force/force_reason/force_close collapsed to one force_reason: str|None; _force_note normalizes to the truthy audit note the start-work gate and close path consume. Close bypass keys on force presence, not force_close.
- CLI: --reason no longer doubles as the force note (feeds only close_reason); note rides on --force=<reason>; bare --force -> '(no reason given)', identical to claim. Usage/help + gate override hints unified.
- claim internal force_plan_review -> force_reason (no behavior change). txn/import_ndjson migrated.
- PERSISTED status_data['force_close_reason'] key RETAINED unchanged (reducer/schema fold it) -- in-memory param only was unified; NOT an event-schema migration.

Verification: make lint, make typecheck, complexity ratchet (new=0 increased=0), all green with venv. New tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_force_unification_blusterous.py (7 tests) + migrated existing call sites. Broad targeted run 1235 passed; the 19 integration ERRORs are environmental (a git subprocess exit-128 at fixture setup that reproduces identically on unmodified origin/main in this checkout), not from this change.

Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before Submit.

Patchset 2 pushed (Gerrit 1878, commit 8ebad86, same Change-Id Ibd5eb6c). Addressed all 3 LLM-Review advisory findings from patchset 1:

1. (edge-cases) Lib force-parity: transition(force='') now treats empty string as NOT forcing, byte-identical to claim(force=''). Fix in _normalize_transition_force: result = force or None (a bare bypass is spelled with a non-empty reason). Test: test_empty_string_force_does_not_bypass_claim_or_transition.
2. (regression) NDJSON import close: reverted to a PLAIN (non-forcing) close. The old force=True was a no-op for an open->closed target (start-work bypass N/A; close gate keyed on unset force_close), so passing no force preserves exact origin/main behavior instead of newly bypassing the completion gate. Comment updated to explain.
3. (tests) force_close/force precedence: explicit unified force now WINS over the deprecated force_close alias when both are supplied (force_close only applies when force absent); the alias still warns. Test: test_force_wins_over_force_close_when_both_supplied.

Local: make lint (incl. complexity ratchet), make typecheck, and the affected suites all green with the venv; new suite now 9 tests.

Patchset 1 CI note: LLM-Review+1 (PASS) landed; Verified-1 was a SINGLE macOS py3.13 failure in tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py::test_artifact_create_or_reuse_failure_never_fails_the_review -- a FileNotFoundError from a rebar-gate-snapshots tmp/build rename race in the code-review-gate SNAPSHOT machinery under xdist, an unrelated pre-existing macOS concurrency flake (all three Ubuntu pytest jobs passed). My diff does not touch that subsystem. Watching patchset 2 to see whether it recurs.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PS1 advisory RCA / contract archaeology (2026-08-18):

1. NDJSON close regression — CONFIRMED defect. Import commit 6f701958b7c (2026-06-17) introduced `transition_compute(..., force=True)` as a child-order safety net. The completion close gate was added one day later in 85a77b9cc8 and deliberately keyed its bypass only on `force_close`; therefore importer `force=True` never bypassed completion verification. Commit 0f5dbc88b9 (ticket halfwhite-chordal-stonefly) later revisited this exact call to add mandatory `close_class` while retaining the no-force-close behavior and per-row fail-open. Runtime against pristine PS1 fe4281e07c with the close gate ON and a marker verifier showed the imported task CLOSED, marker calls=0, warnings=[]: the mechanical migration to `force_reason="ndjson import safety net"` accidentally expanded authority. Expected repair: omit force on importer closes; ordinary close-gate policy remains in force and a refused close remains an import warning/open row.

2. Empty-string parity — CONFIRMED incomplete implementation against the approved universal library contract `force: str | None`, where only None means absent and any string is a supplied force reason. Claim CLI archaeology (82186374d7 and current `_parse_force`) already converts bare/`--force=` to `(no reason given)` so bypasses are never audit-empty. Runtime against PS1 showed `claim(force="")` BLOCKED/open while `transition(force="")` BYPASSED/in_progress: `_lib_writes.claim` erased presence via `force or ""`, while transition preserved the string and `_force_note` supplied the placeholder. Expected repair: preserve presence on both verbs and normalize an empty supplied reason to `(no reason given)`; do not collapse it to None.

3. Deprecated-alias precedence — CONFIRMED defect. PS1 `_normalize_transition_force` assigns `force_close` last, so the retired alias overwrites the canonical explicit `force`. Runtime with `force="canonical", force_close="legacy"` recorded only `legacy`. The migration contract makes `force_close` a compatibility alias, and the repository-wide explicit-input convention is canonical explicit input wins (e.g. operation snapshot/config override contracts); an alias must fill only when canonical force is absent. Preserve old `force=False, force_close=x` compatibility, while treating every string including empty as an explicit canonical value.

4. Documentation — CONFIRMED stale current guidance. CHANGELOG.md:128 and docs/release-notes.md:288 come from the 0.12 CLI-only rename (63db6ac5a8) and say the library `force_close` kwarg is unchanged. PS1 now deprecates/maps that kwarg to `force`, so newest-first contract notes and the Unreleased changelog must announce the library normalization while the 0.12 historical entry is contextualized rather than left as current advice.

Caller/safety sweep: transition/claim share the command core; automated NDJSON import is the one behavioral dependency on the old split and must remain an ordinary close. MCP transition remains deliberately sequenced in dependent ticket scratchy-leprous-galago; no change here. No new dependency or capability is required. Next: final-form behavioral RED tests for all three executable mechanisms, then focused GREEN + exact-defect mutations and full gates.

comments.body:
Advisory repair + rebase report (Gerrit 1878 PS3, d8fac8981bdcd6f415f2ab3ee19957d03448d55b):

Problem: PS1 unified force plumbing but accidentally expanded NDJSON authority, diverged on empty-string force, let a deprecated alias override canonical input, and left current contract guidance stale.

Proven causes / proof:
- NDJSON: pre-unification `force=True` only armed start-work; completion bypass was separately keyed on `force_close` since gate-introduction commit 85a77b9cc8. PS1 mapped it to unified force, so runtime closed without calling a marker verifier.
- Empty string: claim erased presence via `force or ""`; transition preserved it and `_force_note` used the placeholder. PS1 runtime: claim BLOCKED/open, transition BYPASSED/in_progress. Approved contract is None=absent, any string=present reason.
- Precedence: PS1 assigned deprecated `force_close` last. Runtime with canonical=`canonical`, alias=`legacy` recorded only `legacy`; compatibility aliases must fill only when canonical input is absent.
- Docs/help: the 0.12 CLI-only release prose and packaged transition help still described pre-normalization behavior.

RED→GREEN oracles:
- `test_empty_string_force_bypasses_claim_and_transition_identically`: final RED on PS1 at claim gate; GREEN with both verbs in_progress and identical `(no reason given)` audits. Exact `force or ""` mutation returned RED.
- `test_force_wins_over_force_close_when_both_supplied`: final RED recorded `legacy loses`; GREEN records `new wins` while still warning. Unconditional-alias mutation returned RED.
- `test_imported_close_respects_completion_verification_gate`: final RED had zero verifier calls and a closed import; GREEN calls the marker verifier, leaves the row open, and reports the per-row warning. Re-adding unified importer force returned RED.
- `test_transition_help_keeps_reason_separate_from_force`: final RED on packaged PS1 help; GREEN after source help correction + generated CLI reference refresh.
All oracles are observable state/audit/help contracts and remain insensitive to private refactors.

Fix / safety:
- `_normalize_transition_force` distinguishes canonical string presence from both legacy spellings; explicit canonical input wins, including empty string. `claim(force="")` now emits the same audit-safe placeholder as transition/bare CLI force.
- NDJSON omits force on replay closes, preserving target close policy and its established per-row fail-open warning behavior.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased + newest-first release notes announce the library migration while preserving 0.12 historical context. Packaged help is the source; `docs/cli-reference.md` was regenerated and `--check` is clean.
- No new dependency/capability, no weakened assertion, persisted `force_close_reason` unchanged, unresolved-child invariant unchanged.

Sibling/parity sweep:
- CLI, library, automated NDJSON, packaged help, generated reference, changelog, and release notes checked. The stale packaged-help sibling was fixed in scope. MCP transition remains deliberately sequenced in dependent ticket scratchy-leprous-galago; no accidental MCP change here. No other live `transition --force --reason` / current-force-note guidance found outside historical fixtures/experiments.

Verification:
- Rebased directly onto merged 1877 `b34a26c83d`; parent SHA check proves 1877 preserved exactly.
- Expanded lifecycle/import/deprecation/disposition/help/generator suite green (including the new oracles).
- `make lint` green; `make typecheck` green (560 files); complexity `active=51 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`; generated CLI reference check green; `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` resolves canonical ticket.
- Pushed Gerrit 1878 PS3. Fresh LLM/Verified gates pending; DO NOT submit until both +1 and zero unresolved comments. PS1 Verified-1 was the independent shared gate-snapshot race (`test_artifact_create_or_reuse_failure_never_fails_the_review`, missing temp snapshot rename source), not a force-path test; the parent debug loop already owns the snapshot-race dependency and must sequence landing/rebase if PS3 reproduces it.

compiled_state.description:
Normalize the force-bypass surface so `--force[=<reason>]` is the single approved pattern across `transition` and `claim`, consistently across the externally-exposed surfaces (CLI + library) AND the internal module/method naming, and remove the redundant `force_close`.

Operator rulings (2026-08-18): `--force[=<reason>]` is the universal approved pattern — the audit reason is tightly coupled to the force operation, so it rides on `--force`, NOT a separate `--reason`; `force_close` is to be removed; blast radius is limited to `transition` + `claim` (tracker-maintenance / init / gates keep their own `--force` conventions and are out of scope).

## Context / Problem
`claim` already has the target shape: lib `claim(force: str | None = None)` where the value IS the audit reason (bare CLI `--force` -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason). `transition` diverges: lib `transition(force: bool, reason: str, force_close: str | None)` splits the one concept across a bool `force`, a separate `reason`, and a redundant `force_close` str; and the transition CLI additionally lets `--reason` stand in as the force-bypass audit note (transition.py help ~lines 42-46, 59-63) — a coupling `claim` does not have. Internally the single concept "the force-bypass reason" is spelled four ways: `force_reason` (CLI `_parse_flags`), `force_close` (lib param), `force_close_reason` (txn.py plumbing + a PERSISTED `status_data` key), and `force_plan_review` (claim_compute).

## Approach
Make `transition` match `claim`'s canonical shape and unify the internal names.
- Lib: change `transition` to `force: str | None = None` (the audit reason; None = not forcing; any string incl. "(no reason given)" = force, bypassing whichever gate THIS transition hits — start-work OR completion-verify close). REMOVE the `force: bool` and `force_close` params. `reason` remains ONLY for its close_reason role (reason-required non-force closes); it no longer doubles as the force-bypass note.
- Migration: a legacy `rebar.transition(force_close="<r>")` call WARNs via the sanctioned lib-kind deprecation alias (rebar._deprecations `_KINDS` includes `lib`) and maps to `force="<r>"`; a legacy `force=True` maps to `force="(no reason given)"`.
- CLI (transition.py): keep the `--force[=<reason>]` shape (already present); the force note comes from `--force=<reason>` else "(no reason given)" — DROP the `--reason` fallback for the force note so it matches `claim` (reason stays for close_reason only). Bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)" exactly as `claim`.
- Internal naming: unify the IN-MEMORY spelling of the concept to `force_reason` across transition (`_parse_flags`, `transition_compute`, the txn.py param) and claim (`claim_compute`'s `force_plan_review` -> `force_reason`), with no behavior change. KEEP the PERSISTED `status_data["force_close_reason"]` key name unchanged — it is durable reduced state; renaming it is an event-schema migration and is out of scope. Add a short comment noting the persisted key is intentionally retained.
- Reducer/schema (reducer/_processors_status.py, schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, types.py) UNCHANGED: historical events (incl. the `force_close_reason` status field) keep reducing to the same state.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_lib_writes.py — `transition`: `force: str | None`, drop `force: bool` + `force_close`; deprecation-map legacy force_close/force(bool) via _deprecations.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition.py — map `--force[=<reason>]` -> `force` str; drop the `--reason`-as-force-note fallback; adopt the unified `force_reason` name; update usage/help text.
- src/rebar/_commands/txn.py — thread the unified `force_reason` in-memory name; RETAIN the persisted `force_close_reason` status key.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py, close_precheck.py — key the close bypass on `force is not None` (was `force_close`), recording the force reason as the audit note.
- src/rebar/_commands/claim.py + claim_compute — rename `force_plan_review` -> `force_reason` (internal only); the `claim` lib shape is already correct.
- src/rebar/_deprecations.py — register the lib `force_close`/`force(bool)` deprecation alias.
- Guidance/help text for transition + claim IS in scope: src/rebar/_commands/gates.py (~302-303) currently prints TWO spellings in one override hint — `claim --force="<reason>"` AND the decoupled `transition --force --reason="<reason>"`; unify BOTH to `--force[=<reason>]`. Reconcile the txn.py override hints (~554, 602, 618: `--force="<reason>"`) and the transition.py usage/help so every transition/claim guidance string shows only the `--force[=<reason>]` pattern (no `--reason`-as-force-note wording).
- OUT OF SCOPE: tracker-maintenance, init, and the gates break-glass `--force` conventions for OTHER commands; the MCP surface (sibling scratchy-leprous-galago); the argparse refactor (sibling churlish-fruited-dassie).

## Testing
- `transition ... --force` (bare) bypasses the gate with note "(no reason given)"; `--force="x"` records "x"; byte-identical to `claim --force` / `--force=x` (interface tests on BOTH verbs assert the same fallback).
- `transition ... closed --force` bypasses the completion-verify/signature close gate (same closed-without-signature outcome as today's force-close); `--reason` on a force close is NOT used as the force note (behavior-change test).
- `rebar.transition(force_close="x")` and `rebar.transition(force=True)` WARN via _deprecations and behave as `force="x"` / `force="(no reason given)"` (unit tests).
- A historical event carrying `force_close_reason` still reduces to the identical ticket state (reducer fixture test).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `transition` lib param is `force: str | None` (reason-carrying), matching `claim`; `force: bool` and `force_close` are removed (grep shows no live `force_close` / `force: bool` param on `transition`).
- [ ] Bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)" and `--force=<reason>` -> that reason, IDENTICALLY for `claim` and `transition` (interface tests).
- [ ] The transition CLI no longer uses `--reason` as the force-bypass note; `--reason` feeds only close_reason (behavior-change test).
- [ ] `force is not None` drives the bypass of BOTH the start-work and completion-verify close gates for `transition` (tests).
- [ ] Legacy `force_close=` / `force=True` calls WARN via rebar._deprecations and map to the new `force` string (unit tests).
- [ ] The in-memory force-reason concept is spelled `force_reason` across transition + claim internals; the persisted `force_close_reason` status key is retained (grep + a reducer back-compat test pass).
- [ ] Every transition/claim guidance string (gates.py override hint, txn.py override hints, transition.py usage/help) shows only the `--force[=<reason>]` pattern; no `transition --force --reason=` or `--reason`-as-force-note wording remains (grep).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green; module-size and complexity ratchets respected.
